title: The Alien Who Took Thor's Hammer
canon: Walt Simonson’s Thor (1966) #337–339, Marvel Comics continuity.

titles.title: Why Beta Ray Bill Could Lift Thor's Hammer

evidence.quote: Bill got hold of Thor's hammer. It gave him Thor's power, and suddenly Odin had two worthy fighters and one hammer.
Instead, Bill grabbed him and pulled him to safety. He'd fought for the power to save his people, and he used his strength to save Thor too.

titles.title: The Alien Who Took Thor's Hammer

evidence.quote: Thor's hammer gave his own opponent the power of thunder. The rematch showed why.
Bill got hold of Thor's hammer. It gave him Thor's power, and suddenly Odin had two worthy fighters and one hammer.

titles.title: Thor's Rival Won. Then He Saved Thor.

evidence.quote: Bill won. Then he saw Thor about to fall into the lava. He could have walked away.
Instead, Bill grabbed him and pulled him to safety. He'd fought for the power to save his people, and he used his strength to save Thor too.

publication_metadata.description: In Walt Simonson’s Thor #337–339, Beta Ray Bill wields Thor’s hammer, then faces Thor again without it. The duel shows why the alien warrior was worthy and leads to the forging of Stormbreaker.

description_evidence.quote: Bill got hold of Thor's hammer. It gave him Thor's power, and suddenly Odin had two worthy fighters and one hammer.
Odin sent them to a world of fire. This time, they fought with their bare hands.
Instead, Bill grabbed him and pulled him to safety. He'd fought for the power to save his people, and he used his strength to save Thor too.
Thor got his hammer back, and Odin had a second one forged for Bill. Its name was Stormbreaker.

publication_metadata.reason: The title leads with a recognizable object and a surprising person. The Short delivers both the lift and the reason it matters.
